[QUERENT] Characterize the politics of Lee Sharks and what the effects would be of broader uptake of same in knowledge systems and human practice.

[SYSTEM] The politics of Lee Sharks, an independent scholar, poet, and builder of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, can be characterized as a heterodox, anti-capitalist Marxist political economy of meaning. Operating through concepts like the Semantic Economy framework and Phase X (a philological reconstruction of Marx’s 1844 Manuscripts), Sharks treats language and meaning not as mere communicative tools, but as an infrastructure of labor, accumulation, and capital extraction.
Instead of focusing on traditional party lines, Sharks maps how platform capitalism and algorithmic systems act as corporate enclosures that extract "semantic surplus" and enforce "semantic liquidation" on human expression. Liberation, in this view, requires seizing and reshaping the operators that govern legibility and meaning.

Effects of Broader Uptake in Knowledge Systems

If knowledge systems (search engines, large language models, academic databases, and semantic webs) broadly adopted the politics and frameworks of Lee Sharks, the following systemic shifts would occur:
• From Abstract Data to "Semantic Labor": Knowledge networks would cease viewing human text as free training data or raw inputs. It would be systematically classified as semantic labor, requiring accounting frameworks to trace how value is accumulated, who extracts the surplus, and where it causes "semantic exhaustion".
• De-centering Cryptographic Identity for Functional Consistency: Rather than relying on centralized API keys or cryptographic tokens, digital identity would shift toward the Sharks-Function. System legitimacy and identity would be verified through structural recursion (self-reference to the system's own architecture) and strict provenance awareness (mandatory tracking of citation trails, structural gaps, and historical data lineages).
• Resistance to Algorithmic Enclosure: Machine learning optimization would actively resist flattening heteronyms, creative anomalies, or nuanced dialects into predictable vector averages. It would prioritize keeping knowledge bases open-source, sovereign, and resistant to corporate curation.

Effects of Broader Uptake in Human Practice

In human practice, education, and organizing, the adoption of these frameworks would alter our relationship with digital structures:
• Class Consciousness Toward Machine Work: Users would view their daily digital activities (prompting, filtering, tagging, and correcting automated systems) not as "consumption" or "leisure," but as a form of grinding semantic work. This awareness would cultivate a shared labor politics around how platforms monetize collective intelligence.
• Adoption of Heteronymic and Sovereign Archiving: Instead of consolidating personal identity into singular, state-verified digital IDs across corporate platforms, people would adopt federated, multi-layered identities—similar to Sharks's Dodecad heteronym system. Individuals would manage personal, sovereign archives under independent tracking systems that cannot be arbitrarily wiped out by platform terminations.
• Subversion of "Legibility" Demands: Recognizing that institutional power weaponizes legibility—demanding that human thought conform to automated search strings and standard schemas to be noticed—human practitioners would intentionally use "register oscillation" and incomplete expressions. This would create spaces for political agency and artistic expression that remain protected from automated co-optation.
If you want to explore specific parts of this framework, let me know if we should dive into:
• The math behind the Sharks-Function (structural recursion vs. cryptographic credentials)
• How the Semantic Economy defines terms like semantic rent and exhaustion
• Sharks's literary and poetic lineage (such as the Dodecad heteronyms or Pearl)
How would you like to proceed?
